text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds were dealt a stinging blow in afternoon trade as strong first quarter GDP data from the U.S. sent Treasuries slithering down. Having held firm for most of the morning session, even reaching up to test resistance at 101.25, The June future was toppled by the U.S. data, sliding to a low of 100.83. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.28, up 0.31 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts rocketed in the European afternoon, gaining almost a point and outperforming across the board as Bunds and U.S. Treasuries struggled to make headway. The June gilt future was 26/32 up on the session at 110-16 by 1500 GMT. Just two hours previously it had been skulking below 110-00. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-19/32, up 29/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures recovered after stronger-than-expected U.S. economic figures to settle in the black but traders and analysts said the risks of a decline were mounting. Traders and analysts said the 5.6 percent rise in U.S. first quarter GDP, and a climb in the implicit price deflator should have more than offset the weak U.S. numbers released on Tuesday but the market clung onto yesterday's gains. The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.96, up 0.06. from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and Btp futures surged in pre-May Day holiday trade, ending just off session highs on a wave of shortcovering and some talk of a possible imminent Bank of Italy discount rate cut, although many dealers dismissed the rumours. Market ignored losses in U.S. Treasuries on bigger than forecast first quarter U.S. GDP jump although some said data renewed fears of Fed rate hike next month. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.70 up 0.68 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury price opened moderately lower due to some profit-taking before the government report on first-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP), analysts said. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-28/32, down 2/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.99 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended sharply lower on Wednesday as sentiment was dampened by rumours that investors had sold cash JGBs, there was widespread talk that investors such as life insurers, city banks and trust banks had sold long-term cash JGBs, traders said. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.19, down 0.37 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - LONDON - New issues from emerging market borrowers provided the focus during a quiet Wednesday morning Eurobond session. Bank Handlowy launched a well-flagged $150 million three-year bond, priced to yield 60 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, via J.P. Morgan. Officials at the lead manager were not immediately available for comment, but dealers elsewhere said the bond had been well-received, reflecting the scarcity of Polish paper.
